reason: 'Indusium covering the sorus' relates two parts, and its meaning depends on the part covered (the sorus, the abaxial surface). Without that part it is a fragment, like 'covered' (C240), so it is not a term.
Spathate means subtended by a spathe. Spathe is a synonym of PO:0009054 inflorescence bract, so this is presence of that part, built like 'bracteate' (C205).
Flavescent means yellowish. Colour words of this kind are the value with 'approximately', as with 'greenish' in the approximate-value pattern.
The prefix sub- means 'nearly lanceolate', which the approximate-value pattern covers, as for 'suborbicular'. 'sublanceolale' is an OCR error for the same word.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum of two values (truncated PATO_0000936 – obtuse PATO_0001935)
reason: This is a compound of two apex or base shapes. It is the continuum relation already used for 'linear-lanceolate'; 'rounded' maps to obtuse, which has the synonym roundish.

target: new: coloured markings (punctate PATO_0001512 + colour of the dots)
reason: The word means punctate with brown dots, so the brown belongs to the dots, not to the organ. That needs the colour put on the markings, not a single term.
This is the negation of FLOPO:0991118 bearded, added in the previous review. The throat or margin is the part of the corolla it applies to.
This is 'caulescent' (rule C344, stem present) with a short stem. The 'short' can be added as decreased length of the stem if a pattern for presence plus size is wanted.
Squamiform means scale-like. As the note on FLOPO:0991143 says, 'leaves squamiform' should stay with rule C145 (scale leaf present); bracts take scale-like.
The prefix sub- means 'nearly fusiform', which is the approximate-value pattern.
A fragment that means nothing without its division word ('twice pinnatifid', 'twice compound'). The quality is carried by that whole phrase.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum of two values (conical PATO_0002021 – mammillate, no term)
reason: A compound shape of the moss operculum: conical with a small nipple-like tip. Its conical part maps to PATO, but mammillate has no term, and 6 statements do not justify one.
Leaves densely inserted on the stem are crowded, which is the opposite of the 'lax' rule (loose, C169). 'Sparsely inserted' in the same statement is the alternative.
A gymnostomous moss capsule has no peristome, so this is absence of PO:0030042, built like 'ebracteate'.
It means a roughly spherical tuber. That is the spherical value with 'approximately', not a new shape.
No term exists for metallic lustre: it is not the same as glistening (PATO_0001373) or iridescent (PATO_0002277). A negated key statement for dried mosses does not justify a new class.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum of two values (linear PATO_0001199 – vermicular, no term)
reason: A compound for worm-like, narrowly linear cells and gemmae. The linear part maps to PATO, but vermicular has no term and is too rare to add.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum of two values (lingulate, no term – ovate PATO_0001891)
reason: A compound of two leaf shapes (continuum). Ovate maps to PATO; lingulate (tongue-shaped) has no PATO term and should be proposed on its own if it is frequent.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum of two values (oblong PATO_0000946 – cylindrical PATO_0001873)
reason: A compound of two capsule shapes. Obloid is the solid form of oblong, so both halves map to PATO.
'Not altered when dry' gives a specimen condition but no quality. It is meaningless without the quality that does or does not change.
'Thickened' is a synonym of PATO_0000591. The bearer is the cell wall, and 'weakly' is a degree word, not a different quality.
A moss leaf part (the hyaline tip that runs out beyond the leaf), not a quality. PO awn (PO_0025349) is defined for grass spikelets only, so it needs a FLOPO anatomy class proposed separately.
A ratio of two dimensions of one part, exactly the ratio-of-two-dimensions pattern.
A position relative to another part, using the relational quality opposite (PATO_0001933) towards the petals.
Plurilocular means having several locules, so it is a count of locules, like '3-locular'. The plurilocular sporangia of brown algae are outside the scope of PO.
French tétragone means four-angled. That matches PATO_0001988 quadrangular, defined as having four angles and four sides.
French blanchâtre means whitish, so it is the white value with 'approximately', like 'greenish'.
'Without buttresses' on a trunk is the negation of FLOPO:0991138 buttressed.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum of two values (campanulate PATO_0104350 – turbinate FLOPO:0991077)
reason: A compound of two calyx-tube shapes, and both already have terms.
Equal in length to another part is the equality case of the ratio-to-another-part pattern ('as long as the sepals').
